The city publishes its own administrative chapter, 'Chapter 1, Florida Building Code, as adopted by the City of Pensacola' (permits, exempt work, appendices adopted). fixtures.basis: Pensacola's Building Inspections page lists the 2023 Florida Building Code (8th Edition), Plumbing, with no local amendment, and its Plumbing Information page names the Florida Building Code, Plumbing as the prevailing code. The Florida Building Commission's report of local technical amendments to the 8th Edition Plumbing volume (local governments must send technical amendments to the Commission, s. 553.73(4), F.S.) lists only Broward County, the Pinellas County Construction Licensing Board and Miami-Dade County; neither Pensacola nor Escambia County appears. The city's own Chapter 1 changes administrative sections only. The state pack's counts stand.
fixtures.quote: PLUMBING Local Amendments To the 8th Edition 2023 Florida Building Code [jurisdictions listed: Broward County; Pinellas County Construction Licensing Board; Miami-Dade]
fixtures.confidence_note: Pensacola's Code of Ordinances on Municode was not read (403). The Commission report was prepared for the June 2025 comment period of the 9th Edition code development and was read from the copy another agent downloaded today.

permit.exempt_list_quote: [A] 105.2 Work exempt from permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction, to include work in any special flood hazard area. [...] Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet (11 m2). 2. Oil derricks. 3. Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet (1219 mm) in height [...]. 4. Water tanks supported directly on grade [...]. 5. Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches (762 mm) above adjacent grade, and not over any basement or story below and are not located within the City right of way or part of an accessible route. 6. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. Exception: Any of the above that are part of an alteration, new building, kitchen or bathroom remodel, or any other project that as a whole needs to have a permit. 7. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 8. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy [...]. 9. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. 10. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. 11. Window awnings [...] of Groups R-3 and U occupancies. 12. Non fixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height. [...] Plumbing: 1. The stopping of leaks in drains, water, soil, waste or vent pipe [...]. 2. The clearing of stoppages or the repairing of leaks in pipes, valves or fixtures and the removal and reinstallation of water closets, provided such repairs do not involve or require the replacement or rearrangement of valves, pipes or fixtures. [...] [A] 105.2.2 Minor repairs. Ordinary minor repairs may be made with the approval of the building official without a permit, provided the repairs do not include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load-bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress [...]
permit.note: Toilet partitions or compartments are not named. The word 'partitions' appears in item 12, which covers only 'non fixed and movable' partitions up to 5 ft 9 in high (toilet partitions are anchored to the floor, wall or ceiling), and in the minor-repairs clause in the sense of a wall. Item 6 exempts finish work unless it is part of a bathroom remodel or another project that needs a permit. The document is the copy linked from the city's forms page (PDF created April 5, 2021).
permit.second_quote: When do I need an alteration permit? Alteration permits are required for kitchen and bathroom remodels in which all cabinets and plumbing, gas, and/or electrical fixtures are being removed. Alteration Permits are also required if the sheetrock will be removed to rough in subtrades or walls will be added or removed.
permit.third_quote: To confirm the need for a permit or required contractor, please check that the address is in the correct jurisdiction, then e-mail us the address and brief description of the project.
permit.faq_note: The FAQ's own answer to 'What projects are exempt from a needing permit?' now covers only the July 1, 2026 exemption for work under $7,500 on single-family dwellings (s. 553.79, F.S.), which does not apply to commercial restrooms.

restrooms_city.note: No Pensacola ordinance or code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found (one web search; the city's adopted codes are the Florida Building Code without local technical amendments). The Code of Ordinances on Municode could not be opened, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

sales_tax.quote: On November 3, 2026, voters in Escambia County approved a ballot referendum extending the expiration date of Escambia County's 1% local government infrastructure surtax from December 31, 2028, to December 31, 2038. The total state and local sales and use tax rate for Escambia County will continue to be 7.5%. The total rate for Escambia County is composed of Florida's 6% state sales and use tax, a 0.5% school capital outlay surtax, and a 1% local government infrastructure surtax.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Pensacola job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Gulf Coast humidity and see the local rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Pensacola offices, schools, hospitals and hotels, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Florida's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Pensacola applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on December 31, 2026:** Florida replaces its building rules with a new edition, and Pensacola applies it to every project submitted on or after that day.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Pensacola's list of work that needs no permit covers painting, tiling, carpeting, cabinets and counter tops, unless the work is part of a bathroom remodel or another project that needs a permit. It also covers movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high that aren't fixed in place. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Pensacola Building Inspections whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_after: In restaurants and other gathering places, Florida can require three women's toilets for every two men's toilets and urinals once the men's room has more than two. Licensed restaurants may be exempt, so confirm with Pensacola Building Inspections. Outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Pensacola Building Inspections sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors register their license and their workers' compensation and liability insurance with Pensacola Building Inspections before the city processes their permit applications. A business owner may pull the permit for a building it owns and uses itself on projects up to $75,000, but not as an LLC. Florida has no state license category specifically for toilet partitions, and a contractor whose work falls in a licensed category needs that license, so confirm with Pensacola Building Inspections which one covers your job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in Pensacola registers a license and insurance with the city first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Florida has no state wage law for public construction and doesn't let cities or school districts set one. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $15.87 an hour for a carpenter on building work in Escambia County, with no benefits amount listed.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Pensacola: 6% state and 1.5% Escambia County. The county's 1.5% applies only to the first $5,000 of each item.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, marinas and waterfront venues:** HDPE or phenolic where the restroom is open to outside air, finishes that match the property in guest-facing rooms.
sources: - Codes Pensacola enforces and the change on December 31, 2026: City of Pensacola, [Building Inspections, Building Code Information](https://www.cityofpensacola.com/131/DSD---Building-Inspections), listing the 2023 Florida Building Codes (8th Edition) including the Building, Existing Building, Accessibility and Plumbing volumes, and [Plumbing Information](https://www.cityofpensacola.com/221/Plumbing-Information). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts are the state's in Pensacola: the Florida Building Commission's [report of local technical amendments to the 8th Edition (2023) Florida Building Code, Plumbing](https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/thecode/2026_Code_Development/June_2025-1st_Comment/Local_Amendments/PLUMBING-Detail_Report-LA.docx) lists Broward County, Pinellas County and Miami-Dade County only, and Pensacola's list of adopted codes shows no local amendment. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work exempt from a permit in Pensacola: [Chapter 1, Florida Building Code, as adopted by the City of Pensacola](https://www.cityofpensacola.com/DocumentCenter/View/20905/Pensacola-Administrative-Code-FBC-Chapter-1), Section 105.2; when a remodel needs an alteration permit: [Building Inspections, Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.cityofpensacola.com/3341/Frequently-Asked-Questions). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractor registration and owner permits in Pensacola: City of Pensacola Building Inspections, [Contractor File Submittal Form](https://www.cityofpensacola.com/DocumentCenter/View/29217/CONTRACTOR-FILE-SUBMITTAL) and [Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.cityofpensacola.com/3341/Frequently-Asked-Questions). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Escambia County: Florida Department of Revenue, [TIP 26A01-16, Escambia County Surtax Rate Update (November 20, 2026)](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/Documents/TIP_26A01-16.pdf), [Form DR-15DSS, Discretionary Sales Surtax Information for Calendar Year 2026](https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/dr15dss_26.pdf) and [Discretionary Sales Surtax](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/discretionary.aspx) for the $5,000 limit. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Escambia County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination FL20260203, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/FL20260203/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023): Building, Plumbing and Accessibility volumes, in force since December 31, 2023 and enforced in Pensacola without local technical amendments; replaced by the 9th Edition (2026), which Pensacola applies to projects submitted on or after December 31, 2026; Chapter 1 of the Florida Building Code as adopted by the City of Pensacola, Section 105.2, for work exempt from permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for Florida's code.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions needs a Pensacola permit (Building Inspections, 850-436-5600, or inspections@cityofpensacola.com).

Update on December 31, 2026: the 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code applies in Pensacola to projects submitted from that day. Rewrite the 'New rules' bullet and recheck the stall table against the published 9th Edition and the city's Building Code Information list.

The city's Chapter 1 (the list of work exempt from permits) is the copy linked from the Building Inspections forms page, a PDF created in April 2021: ask Building Inspections whether it is the current version.
Pensacola's Code of Ordinances on Municode could not be opened: read the buildings title once in a browser to confirm there is no local technical amendment and no city restroom-sign rule.
Sales tax: 7.5% confirmed by TIP 26A01-16 after the November 3, 2026 referendum, which extended the county's 1% surtax to December 31, 2038; read the 2027 Form DR-15DSS when the Department posts it.
The federal wage determination lists no benefits amount (0.00) for carpenters in Escambia County, and its rate comes from a 2014 survey published in 2016.
The Department of Revenue doesn't say whether toilet partitions count as a building fixture or as goods, which decides how an installed job is taxed (same open question as Miami).
The city-base entry lists no nearby cities for Pensacola, so the 'Nearby cities we deliver to' section has no city names.
